speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your dizziness, nausea, and imbalance, I need to ask a few questions. Can you describe the nature of the dizziness? Does the room feel like it is spinning, or do you feel lightheaded and faint?

text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you have denied auditory symptoms, this points toward vestibular neuritis rather than labyrinthitis. I will now request a Dix-Hallpike maneuver and an audiogram to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike_Manoeuvre REQUEST TEST: Audiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dix-Hallpike maneuver: Negative (laying the patient flat rapidly with head turned to each side does not provoke symptoms). Audiogram: Bilateral decreased hearing sensitivity.

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative Dix-Hallpike rules out BPPV, and the bilateral hearing loss suggests labyrinthitis or a central cause rather than vestibular neuritis. Given the recent viral illness, I will request an MRI of the brain to rule out central pathology like stroke or MS before finalizing the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain: No acute abnormalities noted, specifically no signs of stroke or significant lesions.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI rules out central causes, and the bilateral hearing loss with vertigo following a viral illness is classic for labyrinthitis. I have enough information to conclude the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Labyrinthitis
